summary: The authors and HypoExplorer compared the same eight hypothalamus libraries using a sex-adjusted middle-aged-minus-young contrast. All three published age effects agreed in direction: CHRNA1 was higher in middle age, while EBF3 and SLC18A2 were lower. The largest difference was 0.0277 log2 units. Three pairs fall below the 30-pair concordance minimum. [Published age table](https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41467-020-14368-z/MediaObjects/41467_2020_14368_MOESM5_ESM.xlsx)
openIssues: The full hypothalamus age-effect table and per-gene author FDR values were not located. Genome-wide agreement and FDR overlap remain unassessed.

The GEO count matrix matches its historical checksum. The current SOFT metadata file has a different compressed checksum, although all eight registered libraries and their donor, age and sex assignments were confirmed.
